_provenance.measured_against: knowledgator/gliner-pii-base-v1.0, pinned revision 61726e0ad791dcab3e29339bbec3ad42ded65641 (gliner_provisioning.GLINER_REPO_REVISION), loaded via GlinerOnnxClassifier.classify_span with the shipped two-label set (person, organization) -- l3_gliner._GLINER_LABELS
_provenance.measurement_authenticity: The agent sandbox that authored this fixture has neither the `gliner` extra installed nor the model provisioned, so it structurally cannot run GlinerOnnxClassifier itself -- an in-sandbox 'measurement' would necessarily be an assumed/guessed label, not a real one. Per issue #281's own maintainer-step instruction ('not completable against a mocked classifier -- stop and escalate'), the actual measurement was taken by a trusted maintainer on real, GLiNER-provisioned hardware (gliner 0.2.27, onnxruntime 1.27.0, pinned revision 61726e0ad791dcab3e29339bbec3ad42ded65641), reproducing this fixture's own stated methodology exactly: each `sentence` through select_candidate_spans (no allowlist), then GlinerOnnxClassifier.classify_span on the resulting CandidateSpan. Result: 37 of 39 recorded gliner_label values were confirmed as-is; 2 were wrong (Kubernetes and Teams, both recorded 'none' but measured 'organization', deterministic across 3 consecutive runs) and have been corrected in this file accordingly. Every other probe, including every 'seeded' decision and every person-labelled exclusion, reproduced exactly and is unchanged.
_provenance.methodology: Each token appears in one realistic coding-agent-shaped sentence (the shapes ADR-0049's live finding came from: a prose sentence naming a public tool/product/component). Each sentence was run through select_candidate_spans (no allowlist) to obtain the real CandidateSpan Position A itself would build, then GlinerOnnxClassifier.classify_span(candidate) recorded the actual label -- not a guess, the measurement. 'none' means GLiNER did not flag the token as an entity at all (no false positive to curate). Selection covered two shapes: public-software/product identifiers (the issue's own ask) and common-English-word product names one order riskier (the 'ambiguous-word' category), to find the boundary case the curation rule has to draw.
_provenance.curation_rule: ADR-0023/ADR-0032: seeded only if a genuinely public, non-sensitive identifier, implausible as a protected referent when unregistered. A confirmed organization/person false positive is NOT seeded when the bare token is also a common English dictionary word, a known personal surname, or a place name with no single dominant public-brand reading -- seeding is permanent novelty-discovery loss for that literal token in every future context, not just this measurement's sentence. Two probes (Kafka, Jenkins) are the sharpest instance: both are real, common human surnames, and GLiNER's own label ('person') independently corroborates the collision risk this rule exists to catch.

probes.sentence: OpenBao Transit handles the key wrapping.
probes.rationale: Issue #281's own cited live finding (ADR-0033 update): 'Transit' names OpenBao's/Vault's key-wrapping secrets engine, a term this project's own key custody documentation depends on. Confirmed public product-component identifier. Note: 'Transit' was previously in test_seeded_allowlist.py's _CURATION_REJECTS (issue #87, 2026-07-10 batch) as a generic-word rejection made without this specific product context; this measurement supersedes that call for the reason the issue itself gives -- the 2026-07-10 rejection considered 'Transit' as bare generic prose, not as OpenBao's own named component this project ships documentation about.

probes.sentence: Docker builds the image before every deploy.
probes.rationale: Purpose-built brand identifier for the containerization platform; the archaic common-noun sense (a dock worker) is dead in modern usage. Same evidentiary class as the existing seed's Github/Slack/Postgres.

probes.rationale: Not an English dictionary word at all; unambiguous purpose-coined identifier for the web server.

probes.rationale: Coined brand name, not a dictionary word and not a known given/family name -- GLiNER's 'person' label here is a type-classification miss (still resolved to is_entity=true either way under Position A), not evidence of real personal-name collision.

probes.sentence: We store secrets in Vault before deploying.
probes.rationale: Ordinary English dictionary word (a bank/security vault) with no single dominant public-brand reading in isolation -- highly plausible as an internal project/product codename ('Project Vault'). Leaving it out per the issue's own instruction: when in doubt, leave it out.

probes.sentence: Kafka streams the events to the downstream consumers.
probes.rationale: Kafka is a real, common human surname (Franz Kafka among many others) -- GLiNER's own 'person' label corroborates the collision risk directly. Exactly the Don/Mark/Stone/Frank failure mode ADR-0023/ADR-0033 name: seeding this token would permanently lose novelty discovery for any unregistered private individual actually named Kafka.
